subject: Math
prompt: A square has sides of length $4$ centimeters. If the length of each side is multiplied by $3$, what is the area, in square centimeters, of the new square?
explanation: The original square has sides of length $4$ cm, so its area is $4 \times 4 = 16$ square centimeters. When each side is multiplied by $3$, the new side length is $4 \times 3 = 12$ cm. The area of the new square is $12 \times 12 = 144$ square centimeters.
